domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m≥2
g is an integer with g≥0
K_{m,g} consists of tuples k=(k_1,...,k_{m-1}) where each k_t is a positive integer (k_t∈Z_{>0})
In the membership inequalities, i and j are integers with 1≤i≤j≤m−1
Case split for inequalities uses: if i+j<m then compare with index (i+j) in {2,...,m−1}; if i+j>m then compare with index (i+j−m) in {1,...,m−2}
Sum constraint: k_1+...+k_{m-1}=g for K_{m,g}, and =g+1 for K_{m,g+1}
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every fixed integers m≥2 and g≥0, there exists an injective map Φ_{m,g}:K_{m,g}→K_{m,g+1}, where K_{m,g} is the set of all (m−1)-tuples k with positive integer entries summing to g and satisfying the stated pairwise inequalities for all integer indices i,j with 1≤i≤j≤m−1 (using the two index cases i+j<m and i+j>m). Equivalently: ∀k∈K_{m,g}, Φ_{m,g}(k) is a valid element of K_{m,g+1}, and Φ_{m,g} is one-to-one on K_{m,g}.
quantifier_order: Fix m∈Z with m≥2; Fix g∈Z with g≥0.

For the definition of K_{m,g}: element quantifier is implicit (k ranges over tuples), with internal universal quantification: ∀ i,j∈Z (1≤i≤j≤m−1) satisfying case conditions (i+j<m or i+j>m) impose inequalities on k.
Existence claim: ∃ an injective function Φ_{m,g} such that (i) ∀k∈K_{m,g}, Φ_{m,g}(k)∈K_{m,g+1}, and (ii) ∀k1,k2∈K_{m,g}, k1≠k2 ⇒ Φ_{m,g}(k1)≠Φ_{m,g}(k2).

payload.statement_nl: Fix integers m and g with m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1, ..., k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: for all integers i and j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}, and also k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously, with the same inequalities and with coordinate sum equal to g+1. Then there exists an injective function Phi_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.

suspected_gaps: I could not construct a globally injective map Phi_{m,g}:K_{m,g}->K_{m,g+1} from the tuple inequalities alone.
Natural candidate maps of the form k -> k + e_t fail in general, and I did not find a branching construction with a rigorous injectivity proof.

result_payload.stuck_point: The main obstruction is that increasing a single coordinate k_t by 1 preserves all inequalities except those where k_t appears on the right-hand side, and there is no evident uniform choice of t that always works. Moreover, choosing t depending on k creates collisions, so I could not establish injectivity.
